chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Water is not heated for the deceased, nor is fire hastened for him, nor is he embalmed with musk.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended and discouraged practices for preparing a deceased person's body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for naturalness and modesty in preparing the deceased, specifically discouraging the artificial heating of water, hastening the fire for drying, and using musk for embalming. It reflects a broader theological emphasis on simplicity and avoiding excessive ritualization that might distract from the spiritual reality of death, aligning with the principle of *tawhid* in bodily rites.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from a number of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Neither warm up the water for the deceased nor make the fire for him, nor embalm him with musk’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from a number of our people who have said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
There is no need for warming up of water for Ghusl (bath) of a deceased, starting up a fire and perfuming the shroud.”’
